policy_title: Return People with No Right to Be Here
stated: The Conservative Party will sign further returns deals, like the one agreed with Albania, to return people with no right to be in the UK to their own countries.

source.quote: Return people with no right to be here to their own country. We will sign further returns deals like the one we have already agreed with Albania.

bearing_set.reason: Returns deals are an immigration-enforcement and border-security instrument; their stated rationale (the Albania deal explicitly targeted organised-crime networks) directly touches crime reduction and national security indicators under O5.

Removing people from the country engages due-process rights, ECHR/Human Rights Act compliance (Articles 3 and 8 in particular), and equal-treatment obligations — all squarely within O9's legal-rights framework.

State-compelled removal is the most direct form of state coercion; the breadth and speed of returns machinery (fast-track timelines, limits on in-country appeals embedded in bilateral deals) directly moves O10's 'freedom from state coercion' indicator.

membership_note: The policy bears on three fundamentals: the safety/security effect of border enforcement (O5), the due-process dimension of how returns are conducted (O9), and the coercive state power inherent in compelled removal (O10). Potential effects on community cohesion (O15) or public finances (O12) are too attenuated and mechanism-thin to clear the non-negligible bar at this stage.
